The findings sum to -1.0: a modest guidance-trim risk from the diesel/oil spike after the 23 Jul guide, which a consensus flat for 60 days does not carry; a Q2 ID line likely below RBC's -1%; and a small offset from Q2 fuel margins. The scaled number is -0.48, from abs_move 8.0 and p_up 47. p_up sits only 3 points under 50 for four reasons: the 4.7-point put skew already pays for the downside, 18% of the float is short and that rose 9% into the print, Kroger held its profit guide through the same diesel spike, and ACI's own Q1 fuel-cost hit implies an incremental H2 diesel cost (~$20-50M) inside the guide's $75M EBITDA range. The two measurements agree in sign and roughly in size.

findings.question: Q1
findings.finding: Fuel costs rose well above the levels at which the 23 Jul FY26 guide was set: US diesel went from $5.13-5.31 to a $6.53 peak on 21 Sep and $6.20 on 5 Oct (+66% y/y), Brent from ~$83-96 to $124 (18 Sep) and $120 (2 Oct), and California regular from ~$5.35-5.49 to $6.23. ACI's own Q1 10-Q names higher fuel costs as a gross-margin drag at +47% y/y diesel, and the guide already needs adj EBITDA to improve from ~-9% y/y (Q1, guided Q2) to ~-4% in H2 at the midpoint (52-week basis). That lifts the chance of a trim or a 'low end' steer above what a FY consensus flat at $1.79 for 60 days holds. Net of Kroger holding its profit guide on 11 Sep with diesel included, management's late-July share buying and RBC's call for a hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cut 2026-07-23 (EPS $2.22-2.32 to $1.75-1.85, IDs to -1.5/-0.5): stock -21.6%. Guide raised 2025-10-14 (IDs 2.2-2.75%, EPS $2.06-2.19): stock +13.6% (baseline history; Q2 FY25 release).
findings.why_not_priced: Stale estimates and anchoring on the guide. Yahoo FY consensus went $1.790 (60 days ago) to $1.792, and Q2 $0.327 to $0.328, while diesel moved ~20% above its level when the guide was set. RBC's quantified preview still expects a hold. Had the street priced a trim, FY consensus would sit near $1.75 or below and previews would carry a fuel-cost line. It is partly priced: the +4.7 put skew, short interest up 9% m/m and ACI's ~4.5-point lag behind KR since 11 Sep show fear in the price. That share is applied once, here, which is why this is -0.8 and not ~-2.
findings.independence: Different documents point the same way: Census grocery-store sales slowing (F2's document, a different mechanism), Advan's note that Texas and California 'softened mid-July' (https://advanresearch.com/insights/the-gas-convenience-business-caseys-drives-strong-earnings-growth-despite-some-secular-headwinds), and ACI's own Q1 10-Q naming fuel costs as a GM driver (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000046/aci-20260620.htm). Against, and netted in: Kroger held its profit guide on 11 Sep with diesel and freight headwinds included (https://www.webull.com/news/15563114485466112). It is macro-to-company transmission that ACI has not quantified since July, so it is sized small.

findings.question: Q2
findings.finding: Census advance data show grocery-store sales (seasonally adjusted) slowing to +0.6% y/y in July and +0.5% in August, from +2.4% in May and about +1.0% for January-June, with CPI food-at-home at +2.2%. Add the IRA step-up embedded in ACI's own guide (~100bp in Q1, ~150bp for the year, so ~170bp for Q2-Q4) and the tougher pharmacy compares management flagged from Q2. Q2 identical sales are then more likely -1.3% to -1.8% than RBC's -1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 IDs -0.8% came with the guide cut (-21.6%); Q2 FY25 IDs +2.2% came with a raised ID guide (+13.6%). The ID line has moved this stock only together with the guide. The closest template, Kroger on 11 Sep (ID miss, ID guide cut, profit guide held), was bought: KR +2.7% and +4.1% over two sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: Slow data the market underweights. RBC's quantified preview is -1%, and Q2 revenue consensus ($18.86B) has only drifted slightly lower. A monthly Census series and the company's own IRA arithmetic would put the street nearer -1.5% if they had been folded in. Partly priced, because the IRA explanation is known and would cushion the reaction.
findings.independence: Kroger's units decelerated on gas prices in its quarter to 15 Aug (https://advanresearch.com/insights/reviewing-krogers-fq2-results-better-beneath-the-surface) and its IDs were +0.2% including ~140bp IRA (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000056873/000110465926106890/tm2625060d1_ex99-1.htm). The IRA arithmetic comes from ACI's Q1 8-K and call, a document shared with F1. This is an industry proxy, not ACI's number. Offsets: a +10bp Colorado-strike base, and a cyclospora outbreak whose 21 states exclude ACI's western core (FDA).

findings.question: Q3
findings.finding: Retail fuel margins were strong through most of ACI's Q2 window. Kroger's fuel profit per gallon rose slightly in its quarter to 15 Aug, Casey's earned 47.8c/gal in May-July against 41.0c a year earlier, and Q2 diesel was +39% y/y against +47% in Q1. The CFO's 'Q2 adj EBITDA very similar to Q1 y/y' (~$770M consensus, ~$0.33 EPS on my bridge) therefore looks reachable, rather than RBC's $761M (~$0.315).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 FY26 EPS miss ($0.42 vs $0.54) compounded the guide cut (-21.6%). A quarter that lands on what management guided has not moved this name by itself.
findings.why_not_priced: RBC's preview sits $9M below consensus on core grocery and pharmacy and mentions no fuel profit; the street does not model ACI's fuel margin explicitly. It is small: fuel is ~6% of ACI's sales (Q1 10-Q, 408 fuel centers), and the late-August/September wholesale spike compressed margins at the end of the quarter.
findings.independence: Casey's 47.8c vs 41.0c, via Advan (https://advanresearch.com/insights/the-gas-convenience-business-caseys-drives-strong-earnings-growth-despite-some-secular-headwinds), and the EIA diesel series for the y/y comparison. Proxy: ACI does not disclose its fuel margin.

outside_window.finding: The Delaware Chancery trial of Albertsons' suit against Kroger (the $600M termination fee plus damages, including the lost shareholder premium; Bloomberg on 12 Oct reports ACI seeks more than $9B against a ~$6.0B market cap) begins 2026-10-19, after the exit window. A ruling comes later. A settlement announced before the trial is a low-probability, large positive tail that nothing found suggests is imminent.

key_questions.answer: More likely held than cut, but less safely than the consensus number assumes. My split: ~35% clean hold, ~32% held with a 'low end' steer (or EBITDA trimmed with EPS held by buybacks at ~$12), ~28% an EPS-guide cut, ~5% a raise. The expected guide midpoint is ~$1.754 against a $1.792 consensus. Three things are new since ACI last spoke (23 Jul). First, fuel: diesel $6.20 on 5 Oct (peak $6.53 on 21 Sep) against $5.13-5.31 when the guide was set and ~$3.7 a year ago; Brent $120 (2 Oct) against ~$83-96; California gasoline $6.23. Second, Kroger's 11 Sep print, which landed after ACI's: units worse on gas prices, but the profit guide held with diesel and freight included, and KR rallied ~7% in two days. Third, the board: Whitman became Executive Chair (8 Sep), the IR/treasury head became interim CFO (30 Sep), and three directors join on 14 Oct. My arithmetic: the guide needs H2 adj EBITDA of $1,767-1,842M against $1,874M a year ago on a 52-week basis (-5.7% to -1.7%), after ~-9% in Q1 and Q2. Scaling ACI's own Q1 statement that fuel costs hit gross margin at +47% y/y diesel to H2's ~+65-70% gives an incremental cost of ~$20-50M. That is real but inside the $75M EBITDA range, so a 'low end' steer is likelier than an outright cut. The consensus ($1.79, flat 60 days) holds a clean hold; the price (skew +4.7, short interest +9% m/m to 18% of float, ACI ~4.5 points behind KR since 11 Sep) holds a meaningful cut probability, roughly where my answer sits.

key_questions.answer: Probably below -1%: -1.3% to -1.8%, against RBC's -1% (the only quantified preview). The newest evidence is the Census advance series. Grocery-store sales (SA) grew +2.4% y/y in May, then +0.7-0.9% in June, +0.6% in July and +0.5% in August; January-June averaged +1.0% and January-August +0.9%. Food-at-home CPI was +2.2% in August, so real grocery volume fell ~1.7% in ACI's Q2 window, slightly worse than in Q1's. Kroger's quarter to 15 Aug shows the same: IDs +0.2% including ~140bp IRA and ~35bp cyclospora, units decelerating on gas prices, and basket items -3.5% (Advan). Advan also says Texas and California, ACI's two largest states, softened from mid-July. ACI's own guide adds two company-specific drags: IRA rises from ~100bp in Q1 to ~170bp implied for Q2-Q4, and pharmacy laps last year's Rite Aid-era script growth from Q2. Offsets are small: a +10bp Colorado-strike base (Q2 FY25 IDs 2.2% adjusted vs 2.1% unadjusted), a cyclospora outbreak whose 21 states exclude ACI's western core, and Kroger's note that early Q3 was improving. Older data the market has had since July: Q1 grocery ex-pharmacy ~-2% with volume ~-4% (Advan), non-perishables -2.2% and fresh -1.3% (10-Q). The difference from the priced answer is ~0.5 point of ID. It is mostly explained by the IRA the market already knows about, so the reaction to this line alone is small.

I bridged EBITDA to EPS from the Q1 FY26 reconciliation: D&A ~$443M per 12 weeks, adjusted net interest ~$121M, intangibles add-back ~$12M, 24.5% tax and ~494M adjusted diluted shares (485.3M outstanding plus RSUs). That gives $0.329 at $770M and $0.315 at RBC's $761M. Fuel argues the CFO's 'similar to Q1 y/y' (-8.8%, i.e. ~$774M) is reachable. Retail fuel margins were strong in May-August (Casey's 47.8c vs 41.0c; Kroger fuel profit per gallon up slightly), and diesel's y/y in Q2 (+39%) was below Q1's (+47%). The late-August/September spike compressed margins at the very end of the quarter. Weaker IDs (Q2) work the other way, so the net is near the priced answer.

key_questions.answer: No sign of a strategic or leadership announcement at the print, which equals the priced answer. The interim CFO named on 30 Sep is the long-time treasury/IR head, a continuity choice, and the permanent search is 'underway'. The three new directors join on 14 Oct, the day after the release, which points to the strategy work following the print rather than arriving with it. The Kroger trial starts 19 Oct, outside the window. EDGAR shows no 13D, 8.01 or 1.01 since July, and in July the CEO called strategic alternatives 'not the primary discussion'. The Whitman-era board raises the chance of a conservative outlook, which is carried in Q1, not here.

premortem.other_way_reason: The stock rallies hard. The FY EPS guide is held, supported by buybacks at ~$12, July-August fuel margins and interest. A Whitman-era cost and AI program is pulled forward. Q2 EBITDA lands near $770M. And the 59.5M-share short (18% of float, 7.25 days) covers into a 'not as bad as feared' print: Kroger's 11 Sep template of an ID miss with profit held, which KR rallied ~7% on.
premortem.question: Q1
premortem.evidence_already_had: Kroger held its profit guide with diesel included (call, 11 Sep). RBC expects a hold. Management bought ~$2.4M of stock at $11.4-11.5 right after setting the guide. Short interest is rising. My own scaling of ACI's Q1 fuel-cost hit puts the H2 incremental (~$20-50M) inside the guide range.

investment_decision.reason: The print turns on Q1, the guide. The post-guide diesel and oil spike makes a trim likelier than the 60-day-flat $1.79 consensus assumes, and Q2 IDs (Q2) probably land below RBC's -1%. But the price already holds most of that fear: the skew is +4.7 (downside paid), short interest rose 9% to 18% of float, and ACI has lagged Kroger by ~4.5 points since 11 Sep. Kroger held its own profit guide through the same spike, and the H2 diesel cost I can rebuild from ACI's own numbers fits inside the guide range. The findings sum to a short lean (-1.0) and p_up is 47. That edge is too small to carry a short into an 18% float short, the setup LESSONS 7 measured squeezing 24-26%, so the decision departs from the sign of impact_sum on purpose.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: The FY26 outlook table. An EPS guide cut below $1.75 citing fuel and consumer pressure would have made a short right. A clean reaffirmation of $1.75-1.85 with Q2 EBITDA at or above $770M would have made a long right, with the short base as the fuel.
